sections.h2: What is the quickest way to move a Port Chester house?
sections.html:
Line up the village paperwork first, then pick a buyer who does not need a mortgage approval. Cash purchases drop the appraisal and loan commitment that usually stretch a closing to six weeks or more, yet the deed, the state tax return and the village records still have to be finished.

Port Chester is an incorporated village inside the Town of Rye, Westchester County, pressed against the Connecticut line. A seller here deals with a village hall, a town, a county clerk and a state tax form in one transaction. The sections below take them in the order a seller meets them.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Port Chester?
sections.html:
The village's own rental registry law calls it the second most densely populated place in Westchester County after Mount Vernon. The Census Bureau counted 31,693 people in 2020 and puts the mid-2025 estimate at 32,303, living on 2.33 square miles of land. Housing runs from one and two family houses to apartment buildings, including the former Life Savers factory, now apartments.

The village grew around the Byram River harbor and the railroad, which arrived in 1849. Steamships ran from Port Chester to New York City from 1870 until the First World War, and the Boston Post Road was one of the early routes through the settlement. Today the Metro-North New Haven Line station and Bee-Line bus routes 13 and 61 keep commuters tied to Grand Central and Stamford, which gives buyers a clear reason to look here.

  • Named neighborhoods include Edgewood, Traphagen and Willett Estates.
  • The Port Chester-Rye Union Free School District serves every address in the village, and the Port Chester-Rye Brook Public Library is on Haseco and Westchester Avenues.
  • The Capitol Theatre and the waterfront redevelopment anchor the downtown that buyers see first.

Winters stay moderate because the Sound takes the edge off. Wikipedia lists average annual snowfall near 30 inches, with nor'easters bringing the heavy storms, so roof, gutter and basement condition draw attention during inspections.

With rent at $2,028 and an ownership rate under half, many buyers here are landlords or owner-occupants of two-family houses who plan to rent one floor. That brings in the village rental registry described next.

sections.h2: Does Port Chester have a rental registry that affects a sale?
sections.html:
Yes. Local Law I-5 of 2023 created Chapter 248, a registry for two-family dwellings that are rented and not owner-occupied. If one unit is owner-occupied or the house is vacant, no certificate is required.

  • A rental registry certificate lasts two years, and renewal must be filed at least 45 days before it expires.
  • The certificate cannot be transferred. A new owner who wants to keep tenants in place has to obtain a fresh certificate on the closing of title.
  • The owner must tell the Department of Code Enforcement right away about a change in status, and the law names an impending sale as one example.
  • The application fee is $75 and includes the village inspection. A re-inspection costs $150.
  • To register, the property needs no open code cases, no pending village enforcement proceedings, and current village taxes and special assessments.

Violations carry a fine of $500 to $5,000, up to 15 days in jail, or both. If you own a tenant-occupied two-family house, ask the village whether your certificate is current before a buyer's attorney asks for it.

sections.h2: What does the Port Chester Building Department handle before closing?
sections.html:
The Building Department issues permits, schedules inspections, resolves notices of violation and handles the Municipal Search Report. A search request form goes in with a check payable to the Village of Port Chester.

The application counter is open weekdays from 9 am to 1 pm, and the office takes phone messages from 9 am to 4 pm. Permit records since February 2021 are digital in the village's Accela portal, while older files require a Freedom of Information request to the village clerk. One question on New York's disclosure form asks whether certificates of occupancy exist for the property, so an owner with an unpermitted porch, finished basement or extra kitchen should learn now what the file shows.

The state Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code and the Energy Code were updated, with the new code effective December 31, 2025. Work permitted years ago was inspected under the older rules, and the department can explain how that affects any permit still open.

sections.h2: What village bills come up when a Port Chester house is sold?
sections.html:
Sewer rent is the one many owners overlook. The village bills it apart from property tax, based on metered water use, with invoices mailed about every three months. A bill is due within 25 days, a 1% penalty follows, and unpaid sewer rent becomes a lien on the real property under General Municipal Law section 452.

According to the village FAQ, when a property changes ownership the village and the water billing authority must be notified before the title closing, so a final reading can be taken and the new owner recorded. Do this early, because a missing final reading can hold up the payoff figure on the closing statement.

Your annual tax bill also carries a Port Chester Sewer Tax collected for Westchester County's treatment plant, a different charge from the village sewer rent. Ask the village or your closing attorney for a written payoff so neither charge is left out of the adjustments.

sections.h2: How is a Port Chester deed recorded and what tax is due?
sections.html:
The Westchester County Clerk records deeds for Port Chester. The clerk accepts a deed only with a cover page generated in its PREP system, Form TP-584, Form RP-5217 and a payment cover page with the fees and taxes.

  • Recording fee: $45, plus $5 for each page and $5 to file the TP-584.
  • RP-5217 filing fee: $125 for residential property. The clerk's example puts a three-page residential deed in one municipality at $190.
  • State transfer tax: $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500. A $404,501 sale rounds to $405,000 and owes $1,620.
  • Mansion tax: 1% on residential sales of $1 million or more, paid by the buyer.

The state Tax Department says the seller normally pays the base transfer tax unless the contract assigns it, and the forms are due by the 15th day after the deed is delivered. Sellers who live out of state must also address estimated income tax on the gain when they file.

sections.h2: What does New York require a Port Chester seller to disclose?
sections.html:
Real Property Law section 462 requires a signed property condition disclosure statement for one to four family homes, handed over before the buyer signs a binding contract. The same statute permits an "as is" sale, so the form and a discounted price can sit side by side.

For a house close to the water, read the flood questions carefully: whether the lot is in a FEMA floodplain, whether flood insurance exists, and whether the basement has taken water from heavy rain or tidal flooding. A knowingly false or incomplete answer can expose the seller to claims before or after title passes.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental registry certificate to sell a two-family house in Port Chester?
faqs.a: Only if it is a rented, non-owner-occupied two-family. The certificate cannot be transferred, so the buyer applies for a new one at closing, and you should tell code enforcement about the pending sale.

faqs.q: Who bears the state transfer tax on a village sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes the base tax of $2 per $500 unless the contract says otherwise. The buyer owes the 1% mansion tax when a residence sells for $1 million or more.

faqs.q: Which office records a Port Chester deed?
faqs.a: The Westchester County Clerk, through its PREP system. You need the deed, a TP-584, an RP-5217 and payment of the recording fee and taxes.

faqs.q: Will unpaid sewer rent follow the house to the buyer?
faqs.a: It can, because unpaid sewer rent is a lien on the property. Ask the village for a final reading and payoff before the closing date so it is settled in the adjustments.

faqs.q: Can a house with open repairs still be sold in Port Chester?
faqs.a: Yes. New York allows as-is sales, but you still must hand over the signed disclosure statement before the buyer signs, and any open permits or violations are best sorted with the Building Department.
